Thanks @lilitkarapetyan ,
a couple of extra bits, please:
- include the turn number in each row
- make it return a unique list of entries (de-dupe)
- provide a client side API call to get this data (wargame API?)
- Call the client side API from Adjudicate Messages List component on gameDate state change,  and output the results to console

> 

Okay Ian, I will work on it now
Hello Ian, I'm still making cgenges.

Thanks for the update Lilit - and for passing the data objects to the right place.

But, in the `TurnPeriod` object, I don't think we need `phase` or `_id`.   Plus, once these fields are removed, we need to remove duplicates from the dataset.  In a _real_ wargame, as the umpires are adjudicating the turns, there will be lots of updates to the wargame document.  These will clutter up the list with unnecessary duplicates.

Thanks @lilitkarapetyan  - we now just need the de-duplicate.

Now that we have removed `phase` and `_id`, can you see how the same `turn-2` message in two times?

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1108513/215716055-c22cd844-a49a-4918-8552-05542bba5b48.png)

@lilitkarapetyan -  I think this should return an array of TurnPeriod objects, please.
can we de-dupe the array before returning it, please @lilitkarapetyan ?

Note: @lilitkarapetyan - I think this should be returning an array of TurnPeriods

Oh, and hopefully the actual `TurnPeriod[]` data, not `Promise<TurnPeriod[]>`

Oh, and a better method name would be `getTurnPeriods`

issues.title: Server API call for `getTurnPeriods`
issues.body:
Turns can be of varying length, with the length changing during a game.

For _replay_ of previous turns, we need to find which events were "live" during that turn.  We can't use `turnNumber`, since a `planningMessage` may cover multiple turns.  So, while we display drop-down of "Turn 0", "Turn 1", etc, - behind the scenes, the front-end has to convert this to something like "Turn 0 [2022/12/03-2022/12/04]", "Turn 1 [2022/12/05-2022/12/14]"

So, we need to be able to generate a table of the start/end times for each turn.

We can determine this data by going back through the wargame documents.  Do this in this way:
1. Find all wargame documents 
2. Loop through wargame documents
3. For each wargame document with `phase` value of `adjudication`, store the `data.overview.gameDate` and `gameTurn`
4. Collate unique table of turn number against gameDate (ISO String)
5. Return table as array.

Suggest the API looks like this: `/:wargame/turns`
